newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer has no plans for OTC drugs.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer has no plans for OTC drugs.

text.p: British retailer Marks & Spencer Plc said it had no plans to enter the over-the-counter market for pharmaceutical products, contrary to a report in the Times newspaper on Monday.
"We are not going into pharmaceutical products...we will not be selling aspirin," a spokesman said.
He said the company, which markets own-brand products under the St. Michael name, was looking at vitamin supplements as an extension of its skincare range, however.
"We are actively researching the market in vitamin supplements, that is a logical progression," he said.
The Times newspaper carried a report on Monday that Marks & Spencer planned to enter the OTC pharmaceuticals market with a range of products under the St. Michael name.
Shares in pharmacist chain Boots Co Plc fell sharply on the Times report but had recoverd by 1109 GMT to be off 1.5 pence at 641 pence, up from a low of 628 pence.
Marks & Spencer shares were trading at 527 pence, up 1.5 pence.
